newsitem.title: FRANCE: Gle des Eaux, EBRD sign $100 mln pact.
newsitem.headline: Gle des Eaux, EBRD sign $100 mln pact.

text.p: French utilities group Compagnie Generale des Eaux and the European Bank for Reconstruction and Development (EBRD) signed a $100 million agreement on Monday aimed at financing environmental projects for municipalities in eastern Europe.

Under the terms of the three-year, multi-project facility (MPF) agreement, the EBRD and Generale des Eaux each typically inject up to 35 percent of equity into projects to upgrade waste and water services for municipal councils.
EBRD president Jacques de Larosiere told journalists that the bank would cover the political risk and rely on Generale des Eaux and its subsidiaries to execute the projects.

The EBRD and Generale des Eaux also signed on Monday the first project to be financed under the framework agreement, an engineered landfill to be built to European Union standards in the central Slovak city of Banska Bystrica.
Investment on this project is 32 million francs ($5.5 million).

De Larosiere said that would normally be considered too small as a standalone project for an international institution but using the multi-project facility, a number of small progammes to "improve the quality of life" could be undertaken with private sector involvement.
The Banska Bystrica concession will be granted to a project company controlled by CGEA, a Generale des Eaux subsidiary, and the EBRD will lend two million marks ($1.2 million) to the project company.

The potential amount for investment under the multi-project facility could be $300 million, once commercial bank loans were added to the initial $100 million of EBRD funding, bank and company officials said.

Generale des Eaux will use its specialist subsidiaries to identify and set up projects with the EBRD -- Compagnie Generale d'Entreprises Autombiles (CGEA) in waste management, Compagnie Generale de Chauffe in energy, and Omnium Technique et de Valorisation (OTV) and Sade-CGTH in water and waste water.

Generale des Eaux chairman Jean-Marie Messier said the company aimed to reach break-even on any project after two to five years and aimed for an operating profit of seven to eight percent and a return on investment of between 10 and 15 percent.

He said returns were better on small-scale projects such as work aimed at reducing leakage from existing water supply networks, rather than big "trophy projects" which needed long concessions to get a return.

De Larosiere said the EBRD was, to his knowledge, the only international financial institution which lent at the municipal rather than at state level. Activity at this level, without a sovereign guarantee, reflected the trend in decentralisation and democracy in the new republics.
